blocks.text: Perch made three fast circuits of the rocks off Edgewater Park. He could still make the water flash blue behind him, but each turn felt harder than the last. When he nosed along the stones for something to eat, he found bare rock. He tried farther out. There was little there, either.
The lake was clearer than it had been when he first met Seth. Perch was proud of that. He was also hungry.

At dusk, Seth and Jenny came down to the quiet stretch of shore in their blue and pink suits. Flaming Head floated beside them, his fire turning gold against the darkening water. Perch rose between two rocks.
“You look tired,” Seth said.
“I had lunch yesterday,” Perch said. “I think.”

Jenny crouched closer. Perch showed them the rocks he had searched. The algae that had fed his speed was gone from this part of the lake. He had looked beyond the breakwater too, and returned with an empty stomach.
“You cleared so much of it,” Jenny said softly.
Perch gave a small swish of his tail. “I meant to help.”
“You did help,” Seth said. “You helped me, too.”
Seth remembered the fish in the glass tank, and how long it had taken to get him back into open water. He had promised to return to this shore. Perch had promised to stay.
Perch looked past them toward the city. “I said I was staying here. I thought there would always be enough to eat.”
Flaming Head lowered until his reflection trembled beside Perch’s. “You can leave Lake Erie and still care about it.”
“There are other lakes,” Jenny said. “Places with more algae. Places you could help.”
Perch made a slow circle. “And no doctor waiting with a tank?”
“I can’t promise what’s in every lake,” Seth said. “But I’d feel better knowing you aren’t hungry here, waiting for him to come back.”
Perch surfaced again, close enough to touch the toe of Seth’s boot. “You’re going to miss me.”
“Of course I am.” Seth knelt on the wet stone. “You’re my friend.”

blocks.alt: At a quiet Lake Erie shoreline near Edgewater Park, costumed Seth and Jenny kneel beside Super Perch while Flaming Head hovers close; Cleveland’s Terminal Tower rises in the distant dusk.
blocks.text: Perch splashed Seth’s red boot, just as he had the day Seth brought him home from the robot. Seth laughed, then wiped his eyes with the back of his glove. Jenny rested a white-gloved hand on his shoulder. The three of them watched Perch make one last bright loop in the water.
“Will you come back?” Jenny asked.
“If the lake needs me,” Perch said. Then he glanced at Seth. “Or if you do.”
Flaming Head’s flames dipped gently. “Take care of yourself.”
“I’m getting good at that,” Perch said. He waited for Seth to smile, then turned and swam away.
The blue line of his wake thinned across Lake Erie. Seth stayed until he could no longer see it. Jenny stayed beside him.

Perch followed the connected waters west and north. He rested when he needed to. Where he found too much algae, he ate and swam on, leaving a clearer path behind him. The farther he traveled, the stronger his fins felt.
One evening he reached a broad, cold lake under a sky filled with orange and violet. On the shore, a wooden sign read LAKE SUPERIOR.

blocks.alt: A happy blue-green Super Perch with yellow fins swims in Lake Superior at sunset, beside a clearly readable LAKE SUPERIOR shoreline sign.
blocks.text: He darted beneath the sunset, found a fresh patch of algae and came up smiling. The water stretched farther than he could see. For tonight, that was enough.
